epic.title: Epic 418 follow-on — workstream F, MCP front door
epic.intent_and_why: Cleave problem-solving from spine-management. Agents lose context to operating the engine; the door moves that cost behind a typed interface. The token delta is a constraint that must not go the wrong way, not the thing being bought.

definition_of_done: A second front door on the checklist engine exists, wrapping the engine's own dispatch, with the CLI door intact.
F's six done-conditions each carry a verdict backed by evidence, a measured negative counting as a complete verdict.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: No engine logic duplicated; gate imperatives verbatim through tool results; settings.json untouched at any scope.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Behaviour proved by running, with every control demonstrated able to fail.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded issue, wave 1 of a three-wave epic; deliberate first round, no gold-plating.

hard_constraints: settings.json is never written at any scope; project-scope .mcp.json only.
The CLI door stays; every uncovered verb keeps a documented CLI fallback.
Engine bugs #439/#446/#427/#443 are held constant across both measurement arms.
Files fenced to the concurrent posix-green agent are not edited.
fixed_decisions: MCP is the current vehicle, not the destination; the seven-over-eighteen tool split is a placeholder.
Each agent gets its own server instance keyed session_id#agentId.
DC5 is counted from the call record, never the engine's refusals counter.
DC4 is a property over every gate carrying an imperative, not a sampled gate.
DC3 requires a positive control before a no-identity result counts as failing closed.

current_wave.objective: Build the door and produce a verdict on each of F's six done-conditions.
exit_criteria: The door exists, serves, and duplicates no engine logic.
Each done-condition is marked done / done-by-different-means / partial / not-met with the evidence that decides it.

issues.title: Workstream F — MCP front door on the checklist engine
issues.desired_outcome: A typed tool surface over the engine's dispatch, with acceptance evidence for DC1-DC6.
issues.useful_now: It is the epic's least-proven piece, deliberately moved first so it fails early if it fails.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: DC1-DC6 verdicts; a measured negative on DC5 is a complete deliverable under the honest-null clause.
issues.implementation_latitude: Tool grouping, argument shapes, delivery mechanism, call-record capture, tracer protocol and n, which prototype code is lifted.
hard_constraints_no_gos: No settings.json write at any scope.
local_unknowns: Behaviour against a real spine with delegation and rework is untested; exc-9 used a four-gate toy.

wave_forecast.outcome: Workstream C — relocate instruction text to the gate that needs it
wave_forecast.why_likely: F makes C's job smaller: once call mechanics live in typed tool arguments, what remains in an imperative is pure 'what to do at this gate'.

uncertainty_register.unknown: Whether the door reduces spine-management cost attributably, rather than moving the cost to the far side of the interface.
uncertainty_register.settle_by: The two-arm tracer at gate g4
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: Not yet measured on this branch; exc-9's numbers are stale (pre-B channel, pre-A2 verb semantics) and were explicitly ruled non-reusable.
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Run both arms with one counting unit identical across arms, order-controlled, counting far-side recovery events too.

uncertainty_register.unknown: Whether the seven-tool grouping holds up on a real role spine with delegation and rework.
uncertainty_register.affects: Whether the uncovered five (skip, reopen, append, amend, flag-candidate) were the right five to leave at the CLI.
uncertainty_register.settle_by: DC1's cold-agent run on a real role spine
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: A throwaway spine was driven to DONE through the tools alone, exercising all seven including waive and attach.
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Drive a real role spine, not a toy.

parked_possibilities: Replacing MCP with a different kind of tool call, which Tommy expects later.
Trimming rich tool descriptions, accepted for now without a control arm.

completed_outcomes: The .mcp.json delivery branch point was probed, answered, and then FALSIFIED at review — the corrected finding is that a plain project-scope .mcp.json does serve a cold headless agent when --allowedTools is passed.
The door shipped: 7 tools over 13 of 18 engine verbs, wrapping checklist_engine.main(), with an empty diff against the engine itself.
Per-dispatch config generation shipped, rejustified on identity/separation grounds rather than delivery necessity.
A code-map staleness regression was caught by re-running the suite rather than trusting the crew's report, and fixed.

wave_evidence.claim: The MCP door wraps the engine rather than reimplementing it.
wave_evidence.expected: No change to the engine, and every tool routing through main(argv).
wave_evidence.observed: git diff against scripts/checklist_engine.py is empty; every tool routes through run_engine() -> checklist_engine.main().
wave_evidence.source: git diff and independent reviewer inspection

wave_evidence.claim: Gate imperatives ride tool results verbatim.
wave_evidence.expected: Byte-identical text CLI vs MCP, with a control that can fail.
wave_evidence.observed: Byte-identical for the sampled gate; the reviewer mutated as_result() to append a trailing space, watched the check go red, and reverted cleanly.
wave_evidence.source: tests plus a demonstrated-failing negative control

wave_evidence.claim: The door is up and serving — DC3's prerequisite positive control.
wave_evidence.expected: A live tool call returning genuine engine output.
wave_evidence.observed: A throwaway spine driven to DONE through the seven tools alone; a real headless dispatch round-tripped an unguessable nonce through a generated config.
wave_evidence.source: server-side artifacts (call-record growth, start marker), not the model transcript

wave_evidence.claim: The suite's pinned red set did not grow.
wave_evidence.observed: 7 failed initially — map/INDEX.md went stale from the new scripts; after rebuilding, 6 failed / 2157 passed / 1061 subtests.
wave_evidence.source: full pytest run, re-derived by the commander rather than trusted from the crew

discrepancies.signal: The commander's .mcp.json delivery finding was falsified at g1-review: a plain project-scope .mcp.json DOES serve a cold headless agent when --allowedTools is passed. The original probe omitted --allowedTools from that arm, measuring the per-tool permission gate and attributing the result to MCP 'Pending approval' — two different gates.
discrepancies.affects: The recorded justification for gen_mcp_config.py, not the build itself.
discrepancies.evidence: Reviewer reproduced it twice against server-side artifacts; the commander then reproduced it independently in a fresh project directory with no prior approval state.
discrepancies.reason: The deliverable is unchanged — per-dispatch generation is still required for DC2 (different spines per agent) and DC3 (per-agent identity keying), which one shared config cannot provide. Only the reason recorded for it changed, so this is evidence rather than a wave-exit blocker.

discrepancies.signal: map_orient.py reports DEGRADED-NO-MAP on this repo although a machine-generated code map exists at map/INDEX.md with an enforcing freshness test. The tool probes only docs/architecture/* and a README/AGENTS/CLAUDE/docs fallback; map/ is in neither list.
discrepancies.affects: Any run in this repo that plans map-first — it plans as if map-blind and hash-pins doctrine files as substitutes for a structural map that exists.
discrepancies.evidence: map_orient returned DEGRADED-NO-MAP with anchor_count 0; adding two scripts turned tests/test_code_map.py red against map/INDEX.md (55 modules, 1047 entities). Independently flagged by the g1 reviewer.
discrepancies.reason: This misdirects the map-first discipline the spine gates at the context step, so it is a planning-truth defect rather than a local one. Named, not fixed — filed as a triage candidate.

discrepancies.signal: The engine refuses to start a gate that is not the active one, so two independent gates cannot be driven in parallel even when neither depends on the other.
discrepancies.affects: Wall-clock cost of any multi-gate plan whose gates are genuinely independent.
discrepancies.evidence: g2-implement refused with 'is not the active gate; start g1-review first' although g2's only precondition (the door exists and serves) was already satisfied and attested.
discrepancies.reason: Strict ordering is a deliberate mechanism and relaxing it is a design question well outside this issue. Recorded as a forecast-level observation for the epic to weigh.

discrepancies.signal: attest is refused on an engine-checked (command-kind) condition, but the projection renders engine-checked and attestable conditions in the same shape, so the agent cannot tell them apart before calling.
discrepancies.affects: The DC5 fumble population — this is exactly the class a typed interface can absorb.
discrepancies.evidence: Observed live in this run's own init gate: two attest calls refused, costing a round-trip. The knowledge exists in EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json's gN-integrate imperative but not in the spine template's early gates, where it is first needed.
discrepancies.reason: Recorded as measurement input for DC5 rather than filed, since it is precisely what the door is being measured against.

discrepancies.signal: The prediction inherited from #424's body that A2 would ship two flavours of advance.
discrepancies.affects: Nothing — the verb surface was typed from the engine as it actually is.
discrepancies.evidence: TRIP_HARD_GUARDED_VERBS = {start, reopen}; docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md already states HARD refuses the verbs that begin work at a gate, never advance.
discrepancies.reason: Falsified before any code was written; the governing launch order pre-empted it explicitly.

repo_state.map_status: map_orient reports DEGRADED-NO-MAP, but that is a tool defect: a current, enforced code map exists at map/INDEX.md and was rebuilt during this run.
